recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce Coverage.sequence or add redundant Coverage.order prose for this seed; any future example-ordering or Coverage.order versus Account.coverage.priority policy change should come through a new FM decision.
issue_request: FHIR-7863 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Financial Management request asking whether Coverage.sequence should convey primary versus secondary coverage. The final resolution added Coverage.order as a 0..1 positiveInt for relative coverage order, while Coverage.sequence remained for renewal sequence numbers and primary/secondary ordering depended on the billing circumstance.
initial_application: Historical tracker batch commit 43806174288e821cb06173a72cde96317186412b explicitly listed 7863, added Coverage.order to the Coverage spreadsheet source as 0..1 positiveInt, and changed the primary Coverage example away from sequence=1. A later Coverage example update added order=2 to the secondary example. Current structuredefinition-Coverage.xml retains Coverage.order after source refactors.
additional_context: Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-12231 covered the same Coverage priority/order family and is already audited on the combined branch. FHIR-15564 later removed the old Coverage.sequence element as part of accepting Coverage.class, so no current Coverage.sequence definition remains. FHIR-27107 and FHIR-43028 later clarified the relationship between Coverage.order and Account.coverage.priority, with FHIR-43028 adding the current sentence that Coverage.order conveys COB order independent of use case. The checked-in coverage.svg tooltip appears stale, but the authoritative StructureDefinition source is correct and diagram-only edits are out of scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scoped Coverage source already implements the seed decision and later accepted clarifications. No source edit was needed.
